image_description: A low-angle night shot of a large radio telescope dish tilted upwards against a starry sky. The dish is supported by a complex steel lattice truss structure. A bright artificial light illuminates the base of the support structure, casting strong shadows. The background features a twilight gradient and visible stars.

The silhouette of the dish edge shows a smooth, continuous convex curve typical of a parabolic reflector viewed from an angle.

There is a slight disconnect in the perceived depth between the foreground support legs and the dish itself. The dish appears somewhat flat against the sky, lacking subtle volumetric shading that would confirm its deep parabolic shape, though this is partly due to the backlighting.
